provenance.description: M5 benchmark: demand skew; high-demand product starts far, low-demand starts near.
assumptions: Open room: no rack interferes with packing-to-pick routes, so packing distances are exact Manhattan distances.
Demand skew 10:4:1 with the highest-demand product starting farthest from packing.
One empty compatible location (L-spare) allows single-move repair.
Benchmark contract: predetermined approved requirements, identical for baseline, heuristic, and model runs.
Manual normalization: any interpreted draft is retained for provenance; approval uses this contract with all questions resolved.

attempts.name: proposal-1
attempts.rationale: Assign highest-frequency products to nearest reachable locations while preserving distinct assignments.

attempts.name: proposal-2
attempts.rationale: Assign highest frequencies to shortest distances: P-hi and P-mid to 1000mm locations, P-lo to 2000mm.

attempts.name: proposal-3
attempts.rationale: Assign highest-frequency products to the closest reachable locations while retaining all products and respecting compatibility and relocation limit.

limitations: Conservative 2D clearance model: not a safety certification or complete maneuverability assessment.
Nearest-neighbor routing is deterministic but not globally optimal.
Bounding-box fit does not prove real-world packability, rack load safety, or handling suitability.
Travel reduction is not converted to labor, monetary, or throughput improvement.
Demand heuristic runs before model proposals with its own candidate-evaluation budget; budgets differ across methods (no equal-compute claim).
Rack meshes are SimReady GLB (CC-BY-4.0, see asset manifest); markers and route remain DEVELOPMENT PROXIES.
